headline: Two Tornadoes Strike The Brazilian State Of Paraná In One Day
metaDescription: Tornadoes classified as F1 on the Fujita scale hit the Brazilian state of Paraná, damaging property and causing power outages across affected regions.
aiSummaryBullets: The meteorological agency Simepar confirmed two separate tornadoes occurred in the state of Paraná on Friday.
Both weather events were classified as F1 on the Fujita scale with wind speeds estimated between 117 and 180 km/h.
No injuries or fatalities have been reported, though the storms resulted in significant power outages for residents.
aiContextParagraph: On November 20, 2026, the Brazilian state of Paraná experienced two tornado events in a single day, affecting the municipalities of Foz do Iguaçu and Manoel Ribas. According to the state's environmental monitoring system, Simepar, these phenomena were categorized as F1 on the Fujita scale, indicating wind speeds ranging from 117 to 180 km/h. While the severe weather caused structural damage and widespread electrical supply disruptions, local authorities reported no deaths or injuries related to the events. These incidents bring the total number of tornadoes recorded in the region during the 2026 calendar year to 15. The storms have prompted a response from state services as the government assesses the damage to infrastructure and public utilities in the impacted cities.
whyItIsViral: The event is being widely reported by three independent media outlets due to the unusual frequency of tornado occurrences in the region this year.
